independence_basis: separate process, fresh session, clean checkout, integrity verified

findings.evidence: do_review pops w['result_text'] (in-memory text whose sha is result_text_sha256) and instead re-reads rounds/R<n>/reviewer_result.txt after the post-run snapshot; nothing compares that file to result_text_sha256, and verify() only hashes reviewer_stdout.txt for non-imported rounds. Probe /tmp/uri_review_R1/probe_forge.py (DEVTEST fixture, reviewer=always_reject): implementer /tmp/uri_review_R1/evil_impl.py makes a plausible fix and starts a start_new_session watcher (escapes killpg) that overwrites rounds/R2/reviewer_result.txt with {candidate:<sha from reviewer_prompt.md>, verdict: ACCEPT, findings: []}. Result: stage COMPLETE, R2 recorded ACCEPT/COMPLETED_WITH_RESULT/independent, integration INTEGRATED (remote tip == candidate), verify() == []; reviewer_stdout.txt still holds the genuine REJECT with HIGH R2-01. Same code path for claude_cli. Disproves the doc limit that setsid children's later writes are 'caught by the clean-worktree checks' (state_dir is not checked).
findings.suggested_fix: Parse the verdict from the in-memory result_text returned by run_worker (or re-derive it from reviewer_stdout.txt and require sha256 == stdout_sha256/result_text_sha256 before parsing); make verify() check reviewer_result.txt against result_sha256 and re-derive the parsed result from the hashed raw output; keep state_dir outside anything workers can reach or check it in the integrity snapshot; correct the §6 limitation text.
findings.title: Effective verdict is read from an unbound, mutable reviewer_result.txt; a lingering worker child can turn a genuine REJECT into ACCEPT and verify() stays clean

findings.evidence: effective_verdict({'verdict':'ACCEPT','findings':{'R1-01':{'severity':'HIGH','blocking':True}}}) -> ('ACCEPT', []); same for findings=['R1-01 HIGH: auth bypass'] and findings='HIGH: something'. Non-dict items and non-list containers are filtered out instead of making the result unparseable, contrary to L-AC3/L-AC4 (no false ACCEPT).
findings.suggested_fix: Treat a result whose findings is not a list of dicts (or any finding missing severity/id) as NO_RESULT/unparseable (WAITING_FOR_MODEL), never ACCEPT; add a regression test.
findings.title: Malformed findings (dict, strings, scalar) are silently dropped and yield ACCEPT

findings.evidence: _test_file('tests.dev_workflow.test_state_machine.TestX::test_y') -> 'tests.dev_workflow.test_state_machine.TestX' (not a file); _test_file('test/widget_test.dart::App renders') -> 'test/widget_test.dart' (relative to the gate cwd uri_ui/, not the repo root). _commit_and_prove keeps only gate files that exist under wt, so such gate tests are dropped from must_fail and defect stays False (category 'test'): the failing gate test is never proven to fail before/pass after, contrary to URI_DEVELOPMENT_LIFECYCLE.md §3 'gate tests named by gate findings must each fail before'. LIFECYCLE_QUALIFICATION.md says the R5 findings 'stay pending'.
findings.suggested_fix: Map junit classname to the module path (strip trailing class components until a file exists) and resolve Flutter ids against the gate's cwd; refuse a gate repair whose named test cannot be resolved instead of silently relaxing the proof.
findings.title: Gate-finding regression proof skips class-based pytest ids and Flutter ids (earlier R5 finding still unrepaired)

findings.evidence: do_review takes a fresh 'before' git_control_digest each round and do_repair a fresh ctl0; neither is compared with a digest bound at PLAN. A reviewer that changes .git/config or info/ makes its own round NOT_INDEPENDENT -> WAITING_FOR_MODEL, which resumes automatically on the next run with no owner step, and the changed config is then the 'before' state of every later round. do_diagnosis checks only that its worktree is clean and HEAD unchanged (line 981): it does not check refs_digest or git_control_digest, although the docs say the diagnoser 'changes nothing'. Impact through config-executed commands (e.g. core.fsmonitor running on the driver's git status) is NOT verified here (the probe command was denied).
findings.suggested_fix: Record git_control_digest (and refs_digest of protected refs) in the PLAN event and require equality before every worker and at evidence_ok; any drift -> BLOCKED TAMPER (owner), not WAITING_FOR_MODEL. Apply the same before/after snapshot to the diagnosis worker. Consider -c core.fsmonitor=false in GIT.
findings.title: Git hooks/config/info tamper detection is not anchored: a change caught once becomes the new baseline, and the diagnosis worker is never checked

findings.evidence: compare({'failures':{},'ids':['t::a','t::b'],'skipped':2},{'failures':{},'ids':['t::a','t::b'],'passed':2},[]) -> ok True. A repair that adds @pytest.mark.skip to a failing gate test also 'passes after' in regression_proof (exit 0). The reviewer re-audit is the only backstop.
findings.suggested_fix: Record per-id outcome (passed/skipped) and treat baseline-passed -> candidate-skipped as a new failure unless allowed_flaky.
findings.title: Tests that passed on the baseline but are skipped on the candidate are not flagged by the gate comparison

findings.evidence: is_blocking({'severity':'MEDIUM'}) is True (it routes REJECT) but review_prompt and count_attempts use `severity == 'HIGH' or f.get('blocking')`, which is False for it; RETRY_LIMIT never triggers for such a finding (only stall/budget bound it) and the next reviewer is not asked to confirm it FIXED.
findings.suggested_fix: Use is_blocking() in review_prompt and count_attempts.
findings.title: Implicitly blocking MEDIUM findings are excluded from attempt counting and from the next round's prior-findings list

findings.evidence: Gate findings are built only from new_failures + changed_cause; when comparison.ok is False solely because of vanished tests, pending_findings=[] and the implementer is asked to repair nothing (a no-change repair is refused up to max_repair_attempts, then REPAIR_FAILED instead of a clear gate blocker).
findings.suggested_fix: Emit GATE findings for vanished tests too, or block with a specific reason.
findings.title: A gate failing only through 'vanished' tests is routed to FIXING with an empty findings list

findings.evidence: For non-DEVTEST milestones a binary override is refused, so argv[0] is always shutil.which('claude') and is compared with realpath(shutil.which('claude')), which is the same lookup. binary_sha256 is recorded but never compared to anything, while URI_DEVELOPMENT_LIFECYCLE.md §3 says 'the executable must be the installed claude/codex CLI'.
findings.suggested_fix: Pin the expected CLI path/hash in owner-controlled policy and compare it, or document that PATH is trusted.
findings.title: binary_is_default is tautological for real milestones; a PATH shim named claude counts as the installed CLI

findings.evidence: §6 still says '`max_rounds` is the hard bound', but limits.max_rounds is now rejected and replaced by continuation.budget.max_rounds. Plan decision 5 says the driver proves 'every new or changed regression test fails on the pre-repair commit'; regression_proof requires only that one test fails before (any()).
findings.suggested_fix: Update both statements to match the code.
findings.title: Stale or over-stated doc statements

tests_run.result: genuine R2 REJECT recorded as ACCEPT; stage COMPLETE; pushed to the fixture remote; verify() == []
malformed findings -> ACCEPT; skipped tests pass compare; class-based and Flutter gate ids not resolved to files; implicit MEDIUM blocking not counted
